admission.justification: A canonical database was built, and the cost of the source that existed only because it was canonical was measured; no text implementation was measured against it. Every knowledge reader, writer and gate now depends on the file layout.

alternatives.option: Text files in Git: Markdown prose plus JSON sidecar files in the memory repository, with SQLite only as a derived, uncommitted index rebuilt from the files
alternatives.reason: Git already does history, diff, merge, blame and review for text, and a derived index gives the same lookup speed at realistic scale.

About 22,000 lines of source existed only because the database was canonical (merge engine, schema generations, snapshots, candidate plumbing, comparison copies), and knowledge was unreadable without purpose-built views.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The record count grows past about 100,000, or writers appear outside Git.

consequences: A mandatory validator guards every memory commit in place of database constraints.
The SQLite index is derived, uncommitted and rebuilt from the files.
The knowledge database is frozen at the cutover and stays only until it is removed; a converted memory tree publishes no dataset.

Once a repository's official memory line is converted, a reopened review of a leaf that recorded only a dataset comparison -- every leaf closed before the cutover -- shows its knowledge sides as legacy-unavailable; no database is read for it (MIK-R25 rule 4).
Per-file Update History is dropped: content history is the Git log, and judgment history is the per-leaf history files (developer direction D23, folded in here).
context: Knowledge needs one source of truth that people can read and that Git can diff, merge and review. The canonical-database design of the KS and ICR masters made both hard, and its complexity was far too high.
